title: The Edge of Evidence
statement: A witness, a city, and a living specimen occupy the near field of what can be named. Above their provisional order, Earth rises into a dark expanse; the suspended mirror asks where observation ends and inference begins.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

actions.title: The Edge of Evidence
actions.statement: A witness, a city, and a living specimen occupy the near field of what can be named. Above their provisional order, Earth rises into a dark expanse; the suspended mirror asks where observation ends and inference begins.

notes.note: Build a layered threshold: lunar darkness as the unknowable field, a sharply cropped city as recorded knowledge, with an intimate historic witness and botanical growth bridging observation and inference.

actions.title: The Edge of Evidence
actions.statement: A witness, a city, and a living specimen occupy the near field of what can be named. Above their provisional order, Earth rises into a dark expanse; the suspended mirror asks where observation ends and inference begins.

notes.note: Clarify the inferred zone by removing the mirror object’s photographic black field, so its weathered disc, small figure, and birds read as an isolated emblem against the unknowable cosmic ground.
Balance the isolated bronze oracle with a second, human scale of perception: an oval portrait will appear as a carefully bounded fragment of knowledge, hovering opposite it in the dark field.

The composition is complete: the black lunar field stages the unknowable, the portrait and oracle establish bounded acts of looking, and the overlapping archive, city, witness, and plant make the lower edge a dense zone of evidence and inference.
